_about.figma_verification: Spot-checked the blueprint against live Figma variables on node 8285:51565 (Buttons). Confirmed: Rubik is the typeface, Primary/400 = #005dac, Primary/200 = #c9e2f8, Typography Jet Gray #2b2b2b, Gray #575756, Ash Gray #b3b3b3, Surface ExtraLight BluishGray #eff2f4, Borders/Dividers #f2f2f2, Disable/Text #b3b3b3. The variable `--color-primary-400` exists in the file, so a CSS-variable naming convention is real.
figma_divergences: Figma exposes a FOCUS state for every button type; the blueprint's variant table lists only hover, pressed and disabled.
Figma documents TEN text-input states (default, default-error, active, active-typing, active-error, filled, filled-error, filled-success, disabled, read-only). The blueprint is less granular.
Figma's `Elements/Icons` resolves to #707070; the blueprint's `icon-gray` is #575756. Not reconciled: the page uses the blueprint value and says so.

Figma type styles are named per platform (DWeb/Header/H1 36px, App_MWeb/Header/H3 14px, Heading/xl-semibold 40px). The blueprint uses a single platform-neutral scale (display-lg 56px … label-xs 8px). These are two different naming systems over the same typeface; the page shows the blueprint scale and notes the Figma naming.
_about.privacy: The Figma text-input documentation uses a real colleague's name as placeholder content. It is not reproduced; the page uses a neutral placeholder.
_about.not_published: The homepage performance metrics (3.75x / 4x faster revamp, 73% design-time reduction, 2mo vs 1.5mo redesign, 20+ designers) are NOT on this page. They conflict across sources and Arushi's own audit marks them VERIFY/RECONCILE. They appear only in the confirmation checklist.

challenge.lede: Three products, built by different teams at different times, each with its own idea of what a button was.
before: Colour, spacing and type were settled per screen rather than once, so the same control looked different in two places.
Design and engineering guessed at each other
Without named values, a handoff was a screenshot and a conversation. The same component got rebuilt per platform.
App, MWeb, DWeb and PWA each needed their own sizing, but nothing recorded what was deliberately different and what had simply drifted.
A brand decision meant finding every instance by hand.
challenge.note: This is the problem the system was built to answer, described from the specification it produced. Historical before-and-after screenshots are not in my files, so there is no fabricated 'before' UI on this page.

principles: Blue-dominant palette conveys reliability. Clean layouts with ample whitespace.
Orange and yellowish-orange accents draw attention to key actions and alerts.
Every component shares the same radius scale, spacing grid and colour tokens.
Primary blue on white exceeds WCAG AA (4.65:1). Interactive targets are minimum 44px.
Design primarily for light mode: white surfaces, subtle grey borders, minimal shadows.
layers: Five written rules that decide arguments before they start.
Colour, type, space, elevation, radius, icons.
The named values the foundations resolve to.
The pieces that cannot be broken down further.
The library, with states and behaviour specified.
The recurring compositions above component level.

dos: Use Rubik for every piece of text.
Use the documented radius scale: 4px for small controls, 8px for medium and large.
Use semantic tokens rather than raw hex values.
donts: Never use coloured or hard drop shadows.
Never invent a colour outside the documented scales.
Never go below the 44px touch target.

learned: A system is a product whose users are designers and engineers. The moment I started treating the blueprint as a spec with versions rather than a document, arguments got shorter.
Named values are the whole trick. A hex code in a comp is a suggestion; `border-input-focus` is a contract.
Five written principles settle more disagreements than any amount of review, because they are quotable by someone who is not me.
Launching a library is a project. Keeping one true is an operating commitment, and it is the part I would resource differently next time.
Four platforms needed four button heights. The system's job was to record which differences were deliberate, not to pretend there were none.
closing: A design system is the product behind the products. When it works, nobody mentions it. They just ship faster and argue less, and the things they ship look like they came from the same company.

contrast.note: Computed with the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula against the documented token pairs, not judged by eye. Normal body text needs 4.5:1; large text and UI boundaries need 3:1.
contrast.claim: The blueprint states that primary blue on white is 4.65:1. Measured, it is 6.64:1, so the system is more accessible than its own documentation claims.
contrast.caveat: This checks colour contrast only. It is not a full WCAG audit, and the page makes no compliance claim.
